docs.dcterms_abstract: 'The d[istrac]tions of the Christmas Week protracted the birth of these lines which my old year's affection intended to bring forth for her New Year's gift. / But though the day was past yet my fervour continued and caused me to give life to this child which, though it be born after the time, yet I presume you will own it. / It waited a while here for your return now I conceive this is uncertain, I have sent it to you not only for a present but for a protection / Be pleased then to accept it and repute it as a grandchild from him who is really Your most obedient son
docs.dcterms_description: 2 Jan 1643: Ashmole, Elias, 1617-1692 to Carter (Mr), fl. 1643 ~ Carter (Mrs), fl. 1643

docs.dcterms_abstract: 'Sir, the many proofs of your former love towards me imbolden me to send you this charact[er] to desire you to make use of it when you see anything suit with it, and thereby to make a message [?] / Sir I have no firmer friend to me then yourself, and therefore in what shall only concern myself I shall beg your pains at leisure to advertise me and to keep it as private as your closest thoughts, whereby you shall add a favour not inferior to any of your former, and infin[i]tely oblige him who already is your deeply engaged serv[a]nt.'

docs.dcterms_abstract:
'Sir

'I am to acquaint you that my wife going out of the house with a woman her neighbour in her garden to gather some flowers for her / she casting up her eyes upon the sky there saw that which presently much amazed her / the form and figure of a cross and well beholding it with her neighbour she thereupon instantly sent her into the house to call me out to see a most strange sight / which when I came out I also beheld plainly and most apparently according to the proportion hereupon which I drew out / What this may import God knows / It cannot divine but good delivery from the two-handed sword/

Yours L.G:

'This form in a most clear sky shining from the sun through a cloud in white rays / was most apparent to myself, my wife and the other woman about…. / We beheld it on the 16 of August being Saturday about 4 a clock after noon as we guessed the time of the day/'
